key_insight: RHSIA trains a deep-learning surrogate to predict patient-specific hemodynamic markers for intracranial aneurysms in real time, replacing slow CFD while preserving clinically useful accuracy. This enables fast, scalable access to biomechanical risk indicators from morphology alone.
problem_solved: Full CFD is time-consuming, requires specialized expertise, and has low throughput, preventing routine clinical use and large-scale studies of aneurysm hemodynamics.
method: Create a paired dataset of aneurysm morphologies and CFD-derived hemodynamic outputs (velocity fields, wall shear stress, etc.).
Train a neural surrogate to map 3D aneurysm geometry/segmentation to hemodynamic markers, optimizing for accuracy and inference speed.
Validate on non-idealized, patient-like anatomies and quantify error vs CFD while demonstrating real-time inference performance.
impact: Provides a practical path to translate biomechanical CFD markers into clinical workflows and large studies by enabling rapid, automated hemodynamic estimation; relevant to ML practitioners working on physics surrogates and medical deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: medical image → segmentation → RHSIA model → hemodynamic maps (velocity / WSS)
Side-by-side heatmaps: CFD result vs RHSIA prediction on the same aneurysm surface
Bar chart: inference time and throughput (CFD vs RHSIA) showing orders-of-magnitude speedup
Accuracy/error plot: per-case or per-metric error distribution and clinically acceptable thresholds
paper_title: RHSIA: Real-time Hemodynamics Surrogation for Non-idealized Intracranial Aneurysms
paper_authors: Yiying Sheng, Wenhao Ding, Dylan Roi, Leonard Leong Litt Yeo, Hwa Liang Leo
